entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Jacob the Dacian was a Danish-born Franciscan friar. He achieved fluency in eight languages and fame among the indigenous people of Michoacán as a righteous and helpful man toward his flock. His relics, now lost, were kept for a long time by the indigenous people of Tarécuato who still celebrate his birthday every year. Jacob has been identified as a son of King John of Denmark.
